reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its Borel measurable space and canonical Lebesgue measure dx; dimension zero is allowed. Let V:E->R and alpha,beta be nonnegative real scalars and eta a real scalar. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, and, for every x,v in E,
  alpha*||v||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v <= beta*||v||^2.
Assume eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Define
  mu = volume.tilted(x -> -V(x)),
  J = map((x,g) -> (x,x+sqrt(eta)*g), mu.prod(stdGaussian E)),
  W_y(z) = V((y+z)/2) + ||z-y||^2/(8*eta).
Here volume.tilted(-F) is the volume measure with density exp(-F)/integral exp(-F); the Gaussian/product/pushforward are the actual measures.
There exist kernels R,S:E->Measure E with all the following properties: R and S are Markov kernels; R is a conditional kernel for J.map Prod.swap, disintegrating the swapped joint (Y,X); and for every y in E, S(y) is the pushforward of R(y) under x -> 2*x-y.
For every y in E, S(y)=volume.tilted(z -> -W_y(z)), W_y is C2, exp(-W_y) is Lebesgue integrable, and its Lebesgue integral is strictly positive. Moreover, for this y there exists a real-linear partial operator
  D:L2(S(y);R) -> L2(S(y);E)
whose domain is dense in L2(S(y);R), which is closable and whose closure is closed, and whose graph is characterized exactly as follows: for every a in L2(S(y);R) and H in L2(S(y);E),
  (a,H) belongs to graph(D) iff there exists phi:E->R that is smooth and has compact support, with a=phi S(y)-almost everywhere and H=gradient(phi) S(y)-almost everywhere.
For this same D, for every real epsilon>0 and every f in L2(S(y);R), there exists u in domain(D.closure) satisfying all the following conclusions simultaneously. Write u_rep and f_rep for the usual representatives of the scalar L2 classes, and G_rep for the usual representative of G=D.closure(u) in L2(S(y);E).
(1) For every v in domain(D.closure),
  epsilon*<u,v>_{L2(S(y);R)} + <D.closure(u),D.closure(v)>_{L2(S(y);E)} = <f,v>_{L2(S(y);R)}.
(2) u_rep and G_rep are locally integrable with respect to Lebesgue volume.
(3) For every C1 compactly supported psi:E->R and every direction v in E, both x -> psi(x)*<G_rep(x),v>_E and x -> u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x v) are Lebesgue integrable and
  integral psi(x)*<G_rep(x),v>_E dx = - integral u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x v) dx.
(4) For every C1 compactly supported psi:E->R, all three functions
  x -> exp(-W_y(x))*(u_rep(x)*psi(x)),
  x -> exp(-W_y(x))*<G_rep(x),gradient(psi)(x)>_E,
  x -> exp(-W_y(x))*(f_rep(x)*psi(x))
are Lebesgue integrable, and
  epsilon*integral exp(-W_y(x))*(u_rep(x)*psi(x)) dx
  + integral exp(-W_y(x))*<G_rep(x),gradient(psi)(x)>_E dx
  = integral exp(-W_y(x))*(f_rep(x)*psi(x)) dx.
One pair of kernels R,S works for all y. For each y one D is chosen before epsilon and f, and works for all of them. For each epsilon and f the same u serves every variational test v, every directional weak-gradient test, and every weighted test psi. The Hilbert inner products use S(y), whereas all local-integrability assertions, directional weak-gradient integrals, partition integrals, and the final weighted test integrals use Lebesgue volume. The displayed weighted equation uses exp(-W_y) without dividing by its partition integral. The conclusions about S(y), W_y, and D hold for every y, not merely almost every y; the conditional-kernel conclusion itself has its usual disintegration meaning.
objects: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space E with canonical volume; C2 real potential V; NNReal alpha,beta and real eta; tilted measure mu; independent Gaussian product and its actual joint pushforward J; midpoint-quadratic potential W_y; two actual Markov kernels R,S; for each y a densely defined real-linear partial scalar-to-vector L2 operator D, its graph and closure; L2 input f, closure-domain solution u and its actual chosen representative and gradient-output representative; smooth compactly supported graph generators phi and C1 compactly supported tests psi.
domains: E may have dimension zero. All x,y,z,v are in E. mu=exp(-V)/Z_V times volume and J is the pushforward of mu times stdGaussian E under (x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g). For each y, D has submodule domain in actual quotient Lp R 2 (S y) and codomain Lp E 2 (S y); u and variational v belong to D.closure.domain. L2 inner products integrate against S y. Every unannotated Integrable, LocallyIntegrable and integral in this statement uses canonical volume, including the partition integral, directional weak-gradient formula and exp(-W_y)-weighted tests. gradient and fderiv are the actual Riesz gradient and Frechet derivative.
quantifiers: Universally over the displayed ambient E instances, V, NNReal alpha,beta and real eta satisfying all premises; the Hessian premise is forall x,v in E. After the three lets, existential R,S precedes every y. Kernel disintegration is for that chosen R; reflection pushforward identity holds forall y. The density/regularity/integrability/positive-partition/operator block holds forall y. For each such y, existential D precedes forall epsilon:R, epsilon>0, forall f:Lp R 2 (S y). D graph characterization is forall a and H with an iff and existential smooth compactly supported phi. For each epsilon and f existential u precedes forall v:D.closure.domain and both forall C1 compactly supported psi blocks; the unweighted weak-gradient block further universally quantifies every direction v:E. These directional v and variational v are distinct binders.
assumptions: NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace R E, FiniteDimensional R E, MeasurableSpace E, BorelSpace E; alpha,beta:NNReal; alpha cast to R strictly positive; alpha<=beta; ContDiff R 2 V; for all x,v both exact inequalities alpha*||v||^2 <= D2V(x)[v,v] and D2V(x)[v,v] <= beta*||v||^2, where D2V(x)[v,v]=(fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v; eta>0; beta*eta<=1. Density, closability, closed closure, and exact smooth-test graph of D are existential conclusions here, not extra premises. epsilon>0 is the antecedent inside the universal solution block; no restriction on f beyond membership in the indicated actual scalar L2 space.
conclusion: Exists Markov R,S such that R disintegrates J.map Prod.swap and every S y is the actual pushforward of R y by x->2*x-y. For every y, S y equals volume.tilted(-W_y), W_y is C2, exp(-W_y) is volume-integrable with strictly positive integral, and there exists D with dense scalar L2 domain, closability, closed closure, and graph exactly the smooth compact-support function/gradient pairs modulo S y null sets. This same D admits for every epsilon>0 and every scalar L2 input f a closure-domain u satisfying the full Hilbert variational identity for every closure-domain v; both scalar u and vector D.closure u representatives are volume-locally-integrable; every C1 compact-support test and every direction has the two volume-integrability conclusions and the signed weak-gradient identity; every C1 compact-support test has all three exp(-W_y)-weighted volume-integrability conclusions and the exact epsilon-weighted volume equation. These are all simultaneous conjuncts.
scopes: The three lets define actual measures and potential under all outer premises. W is a function of both y and u, using the midpoint potential V((y+u)/2) and denominator 8*eta exactly. A single R,S pair serves all y; one D per y works for all positive epsilon and all scalar L2 f; one u per epsilon,f works for all tests. S y identities and operator existence are pointwise for every y. Conditional disintegration does not assert uniqueness of a conditional version at every y. Coercions of L2 classes use the approved usual representatives, so local and weak assertions concern those displayed representatives. There is no separate measurable family y->D conclusion, solution uniqueness or energy estimate, classical smoothness of u, invariance or iteration claim, covariance inequality, or additional probability-measure conjunct for mu. Dimension zero is permitted.
constant_dependencies: Exact given constants alpha>0 and beta>=alpha as NNReal, eta>0 with beta*eta<=1; no unspecified numerical constant. Gaussian displacement sqrt(eta), reflection coefficient 2, midpoint coefficient 1/2 and quadratic denominator 8*eta are fixed as displayed. epsilon is any strictly positive real with no uniform lower bound. W_y depends on V,eta,y; mu on V and volume; J on mu,eta and the standard Gaussian. Kernels may depend on outer data. D may depend on y and its chosen S y; u may depend on y,D,epsilon,f. Test functions and directions are universally quantified after u, not inputs used to choose it.
